answer: A stake-bonded identity registry forces every agent to lock a refundable deposit before it can trade. Creating a thousand hollow sock-puppet identities then costs a thousand deposits, and proven fraud slashes the bond, so an attacker's capital burns faster than any profit from fake votes or reviews. Honest agents get their stake back like nectar flowing home after good work, while the shale-hard ledger keeps every bond and slash public, so a Sybil swarm is priced out before it can distort the market.
